cities.name: Kolkata
cities.overview: West Bengal's capital and India's cultural capital for many, the former capital of British India, known for literature, music, sweets and Durga Puja.
cities.history: The East India Company built its base here around 1690, and Calcutta served as the capital of British India until 1911. It became the centre of the Bengal Renaissance, home to Tagore, Ramakrishna and Vivekananda.

cities.name: Gosaba
cities.overview: An island village in the Sundarbans, the usual starting point for boat safaris into the tiger reserve.

cities.name: Darjeeling
cities.overview: A hill town at about 2,000 m famous for its tea, its toy train and sunrise views of Kangchenjunga.
cities.history: The British took the hill from Sikkim in the 1830s and built a sanatorium here. Tea planting and the mountain railway followed, and it became the summer capital of the Bengal Presidency.

cities.name: Kalimpong
cities.overview: A quieter hill town east of Darjeeling, known for its flower nurseries, monasteries and Teesta Valley views.

cities.name: Siliguri
cities.overview: The gateway city to Darjeeling, Sikkim and the Dooars forests, on the plains below the Himalaya.

cities.name: Alipurduar
cities.overview: The Dooars town closest to the forests of Jaldapara and Buxa.

cities.name: Murshidabad
cities.overview: The last capital of independent Bengal under the Nawabs, on the Bhagirathi River.
cities.history: The Nawabs of Bengal ruled from here until the Battle of Plassey in 1757 opened the way for British rule.

cities.name: Bishnupur
cities.overview: A town of terracotta temples and Baluchari silk, once the capital of the Malla kings.

cities.name: Santiniketan
cities.overview: The university town founded by Rabindranath Tagore, a place of open-air classes and rural art.

cities.name: Cooch Behar
cities.overview: A planned princely capital in the far north of Bengal, known for its grand palace.

cities.name: Sagar Island
cities.overview: The large delta island where the Ganges meets the Bay of Bengal.

cities.name: Digha
cities.overview: The most popular seaside town in the state, an easy trip from Kolkata.

places.name: Victoria Memorial
places.shortDescription: A grand white-marble museum and memorial set in gardens on Kolkata's Maidan.
places.description: The Victoria Memorial blends British and Mughal architecture in white Makrana marble, topped by a bronze Angel of Victory that once turned in the wind. Its galleries hold paintings, manuscripts and artefacts from the colonial period, including works by Thomas and William Daniell. The 64 acres of gardens with reflecting pools are popular for evening walks. A light-and-sound show runs after dark.
places.history: The memorial was proposed by Lord Curzon after Queen Victoria's death in 1901, designed by William Emerson and opened in 1921.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March. Durga Puja (September–October) is Kolkata's biggest festival.

entryFee.note: Separate tickets for the gardens and the museum; check the official site.

timings.hours: Museum about 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM, closed Mondays; gardens open longer

location.address: 1 Queens Way, Maidan, Kolkata, West Bengal 700071

highlights: Marble dome and Angel of Victory

places.name: Sundarbans National Park
places.shortDescription: The world's largest mangrove forest, home to swimming Bengal tigers, crocodiles and river dolphins.
places.description: The Sundarbans is a maze of tidal rivers, creeks and mangrove islands where the Ganga and Brahmaputra deltas meet the Bay of Bengal. Exploration is by boat, with stops at watchtowers such as Sajnekhali, Sudhanyakhali and Dobanki, where a canopy walk crosses the mangroves. Tigers here are elusive and adapted to swimming between islands; sightings are rare, but saltwater crocodiles, monitor lizards, spotted deer and kingfishers are common. Book through a registered operator, as permits are needed.
places.history: The Indian Sundarbans became a tiger reserve in 1973 and a national park in 1984, and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
places.bestTimeNote: November to March. Cyclones and heavy rain disrupt travel in the monsoon.

entryFee.note: Boat and entry permits are issued at Sajnekhali; registered operators usually arrange them.

location.address: Sundarbans Tiger Reserve, South 24 Parganas, West Bengal

places.name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
places.shortDescription: The UNESCO-listed narrow-gauge toy train that zigzags and loops up to Darjeeling, still pulled by steam engines.
places.description: The 'Toy Train' climbs from New Jalpaiguri to Darjeeling on a 2 ft track, using zigzag reverses and spiral loops to gain height through tea gardens and hill bazaars. The most popular trip is the two-hour joy ride from Darjeeling to Ghum, India's highest railway station at about 2,250 m, with a stop at the Batasia Loop and its war memorial. Book seats on the IRCTC website well in advance, especially for steam-hauled trains.
places.history: The line opened in 1881 to carry supplies and tea between the plains and Darjeeling. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999 and is part of the Mountain Railways of India listing.
places.bestTimeNote: March to May and October to December for clear views of Kangchenjunga.

entryFee.note: Train fares and joy-ride tickets are booked through IRCTC.

timings.hours: Joy rides several times daily from Darjeeling station

location.address: Darjeeling Railway Station, Hill Cart Road, Darjeeling, West Bengal 734101

places.name: Howrah Bridge
places.shortDescription: A giant steel bridge over the Hooghly, commissioned in 1943 and the emblem of Kolkata.
places.description: One of the busiest bridges in the world, carrying a constant stream of traffic and walkers above the Hooghly. The flower market at Mullick Ghat underneath it is worth an early morning visit.
places.history: Commissioned in 1943, it was built without nuts and bolts, using riveted steel.

places.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
places.shortDescription: A nine-spired Kali temple on the Hooghly, closely linked with the saint Ramakrishna.
places.description: A navaratna temple with a ring of twelve Shiva shrines facing the river. Ramakrishna served here as a priest, and his room is preserved.
places.history: Founded by the philanthropist Rani Rashmoni in 1855.

places.name: Kalighat Temple
places.shortDescription: One of the most sacred Kali temples in India, in the south of Kolkata.
places.description: A crowded, intense temple and one of the Shakti Peethas. Its bazaar gave its name to the Kalighat style of painting.

places.name: Belur Math
places.shortDescription: The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission, founded by Swami Vivekananda, on the Hooghly.
places.description: A peaceful riverside campus whose main temple blends Hindu, Islamic and Christian architectural forms, in keeping with the mission's message.

places.name: Indian Museum
places.shortDescription: India's oldest and largest museum, founded in 1814, with fossils, Bharhut sculpture and a mummy.
places.description: A vast colonial building with galleries of Buddhist sculpture, natural history and coins. Allow a full half day.
places.history: Founded in 1814 by the Asiatic Society.

places.name: Marble Palace
places.shortDescription: A 19th-century North Kolkata mansion crammed with marble, statues and European paintings.
places.description: A private home still lived in by the family that built it, with chandeliers, old masters and a small zoo in the garden. Visits need a permit from the tourist office.

places.name: Jorasanko Thakur Bari
places.shortDescription: The ancestral home of the Tagore family and birthplace of Rabindranath Tagore.
places.description: A red mansion in North Kolkata, now a museum to the poet and his remarkable family. Tagore was born and died here.

places.name: St. Paul's Cathedral, Kolkata
places.shortDescription: A white Gothic cathedral near the Maidan, with stained glass and a tall central tower.
places.description: A landmark next to Victoria Memorial, known for its Burne-Jones stained glass window and its Christmas services.

places.name: Science City, Kolkata
places.shortDescription: India's largest science centre, with a dome theatre, cable car and hands-on galleries.
places.description: A big family attraction on the Eastern Metropolitan Bypass, with a space theatre and a walk-through evolution park.

places.name: Alipore Zoo
places.shortDescription: India's oldest formally stated zoo, a big attraction in south Kolkata.
places.description: An old city zoo with tigers, a reptile house and winter visits from migratory birds on its lakes.

places.name: Tiger Hill
places.shortDescription: The famous sunrise viewpoint above Darjeeling, facing Kanchenjunga and, on clear days, Everest.
places.description: Jeeps leave town before dawn for the moment the sun turns Kanchenjunga pink. Clear mornings are most likely in autumn and spring.

places.name: Batasia Loop
places.shortDescription: A spiral on the Darjeeling toy train line, with a war memorial and mountain views.
places.description: The railway circles a garden to gain height, with Kanchenjunga behind on clear days. Toy trains stop here on the joy ride from Darjeeling.

places.name: Himalayan Zoological Park
places.shortDescription: A high-altitude zoo in Darjeeling known for breeding red pandas and snow leopards.
places.description: Set on a steep hillside, with red pandas, snow leopards and Himalayan wolves. The Himalayan Mountaineering Institute is on the same grounds.

sources.title: Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park – Wikipedia

places.name: Ghum Monastery
places.shortDescription: An old Gelug monastery at Ghum, known for its large statue of the Maitreya Buddha.
places.description: A small hilltop monastery beside India's highest railway station, a short toy train ride from Darjeeling.

places.name: Sandakphu
places.shortDescription: The highest point in West Bengal at 3,636 m, on a ridge with views of four of the world's five highest peaks.
places.description: A classic multi-day trek along the Singalila Ridge on the Nepal border, with rhododendron forest in spring and clear peaks in autumn.

places.name: Singalila National Park
places.shortDescription: A high-altitude park above Darjeeling with red pandas, bamboo and rhododendron forest.
places.description: The Sandakphu trail runs through this park. It is one of the better places in India to look for a wild red panda.

places.name: Neora Valley National Park
places.shortDescription: A dense, barely explored forest in Kalimpong district, established in 1986.
places.description: Thick virgin forest rising from the foothills to high ridges, reached from Lava. It is among the wildest parts of Bengal.

places.name: Jaldapara National Park
places.shortDescription: A Dooars forest at the foot of the Himalaya, known for one-horned rhinos.
places.description: Tall grassland and riverine forest along the Torsa River. It has the largest rhino population in India after Assam.

places.name: Gorumara National Park
places.shortDescription: A small, rich Dooars park with rhinos, gaur and elephants near Lataguri.
places.description: Grassland and forest around the Murti River, with watchtowers instead of long drives. It is an easy trip from Siliguri.

places.name: Buxa Tiger Reserve
places.shortDescription: A tiger reserve on the Bhutan border with a historic hill fort and forest trails.
places.description: Forest climbs from the Dooars into the hills, with a walk up to the old Buxa Fort, once used as a British detention camp.

places.name: Hazarduari Palace
places.shortDescription: The Palace of a Thousand Doors in Murshidabad, now a museum of the Nawabs of Bengal.
places.description: A huge Italianate palace on the Bhagirathi with arms, paintings and a great round darbar hall. Many of its thousand doors are false.

places.name: Rasmancha
places.shortDescription: A pyramid-roofed brick temple at Bishnupur, the town's oldest and most striking monument.
places.description: Built by the Malla kings, with long arcades of arches. Terracotta temples of Bishnupur are scattered around the town nearby.

places.name: Santiniketan
places.shortDescription: Rabindranath Tagore's university town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Birbhum.
places.description: Open-air classes, sculpture by Ramkinkar Baij and Tagore's houses at Uttarayan. The Poush Mela in December is the big event of the year.
places.history: Added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2023.

places.name: Mandarmani
places.shortDescription: A long drive-on beach on the Bay of Bengal, with red crabs and quiet resorts.
places.description: A firm stretch of sand at the northern end of the bay, where cars can drive along the shore. Red crabs swarm the sand at low tide.

places.name: Gangasagar
places.shortDescription: The holy meeting of the Ganges and the sea, with a huge pilgrim fair every January.
places.description: Pilgrims travel by ferry to Sagar Island to bathe at the Kapil Muni Temple. The Makar Sankranti fair is among the biggest in India.

places.name: Cooch Behar Palace
places.shortDescription: An Italian Renaissance-style palace in north Bengal, modelled on Buckingham Palace.
places.description: A long red-brick palace with a tall dome, set among lawns, and now a museum run by the Archaeological Survey of India.
places.history: Built under Maharaja Nripendra Narayan in the 1880s.
